Subdivides the sites of a basin in 11 topographic classes.

**Toolbox folder:** Geomorphology<br>
**Status:** Certified<br>
**Keywords:** Geomorphology, OmsTc, OmsSlope, OmsExtractNetwork<br>
**Authors:** Daniele Andreis, Erica Ghesla, Cozzini Andrea, Rigon Riccardo<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.Gc`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inSlope` | raster file |  |  | The map of the slope |
| `inNetwork` | raster file |  |  | The map with the network |
| `inCp9` | raster file |  |  | The map with the Thopological classes cp9 |
| `pTh` | int |  | `0` | The slope, as tangent like the output of Slope, from which a cell is classified as steep (class 110). |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outClasses` | output file |  | The map with the geomorphological classes |
| `outAggregateClasses` | output file |  | The map with the geomorphological classes |

**Notes**

Each cell gets, in this order: 110 if its slope reaches the threshold (steep sites), 100 if it is a network cell (value 2 in the network map, as from ExtractNetwork), otherwise its class from Tc (10 to 90).

The aggregated map groups them in 15 non-channelled valleys (classes 30, 70, 90), 25 planar sites (10), 35 channels (100), 45 hillslopes (20, 40, 50, 60, 80) and 55 steep sites (110).
